corsten.text: Corsten has been at this since 2014, and the card tells a familiar veteran story: strong in the matchups, with a matchup kill-death ledger to match. The aim and the headshots sit below average; the lifetime board sits below average too. The edge thins a little against the toughest third, the one soft seam in a long, steady record.

couldnotthinkofausername.text: couldnotthinkofausername is barely three weeks in, and already loud: top-tier tempo, top-tier matchup results, and headshots landing top-tier too. The aim runs below average, yet the results keep landing at the top, which says the fight sense is already there. Early read, but the opening chapters carry real weight.

callmemilk.text: CallMeMilk plays at full tilt: a top-shelf tempo, unafraid of stronger opposition, and a direct-duel tally among the best tracked. The lifetime numbers match the matchups, with pace and accuracy both near the very top. One soft note — the edge thins against the hardest opponents — but on nearly every count this is a sharp, front-foot game.

chillinwidem.text: chillinwidem plays a game with no holes in it. Every adjusted mark lands well above average, with a quick tempo and an edge that holds as the opposition gets stronger. The matchup kill-death figures sit mid-pack, and so does the lifetime kill-death line, which keeps the story honest. A steady, well-rounded regular who rarely gives anything away.

congratu.text: Congratu fights with patience and precision: standing well above the middle of the field, measured on the trigger, and holding firm when the duels get tougher. Pace sits mid-pack, yet the headshot rate runs above average, so the kills come from placement rather than volume. The career numbers agree with the duels, painting the same picture twice: a thoughtful regular who picks their moments well.

cobaltpractise.text: CobaltPractise is brand new on the board, so read this as a first sketch: top shelf on the tempo, the matchups, and the lifetime IvI line, with accuracy to match. Unfazed as the opposition sharpens, and the consistency already holds up. Early days, but the opening pages are loud.

cookzvz.text: CooKZVZ keeps the ledger honest: well above average in the matchups, steady as the opposition stiffens, and patient enough to let the fight come to them. The lifetime board reads a shade more modestly, which keeps the story grounded. A dependable regular, the kind who turns up, trades well, and leaves the other side with nothing cheap.

cloudwuulftre.text: CloudWuulfTRE plays a patient, honest game, well above the middle overall. Unhurried on the tempo, and unshaken while the opposition stiffens. The resistance sits above average — the sturdiest part of the game. The aim is below average and headshots are rare, and the lifetime IvI line sits below average too. The head-to-head account comes out middling, a fair reflection. A steady regular still building, with a solid core to grow from.

capatain5am.text: Capatain5am is a walking contradiction: among the very best tracked in the duels that matter, yet the lifetime IvI line sits near the very bottom and headshots almost never come. The pace stays middling, the aim ordinary, and still the matchups keep breaking their way. No flash, no flourish — Capatain5am just wins.

cornkn1ght.text: Cornkn1ght wins the fights that matter and lets the rest go: their head-to-head results against familiar opponents crowd the upper reaches, and they hold their own as the opposition toughens. The pace stays middling and the aim runs ordinary, with headshots scarce and lifetime IvI near the bottom. What carries them is judgment — picking engagements they can finish, then finishing them.

cameltr.text: Since 2013, CamelTR has been a steady hand in a fast game: well above average overall, steady as the opposition strengthens, and ahead in the direct duels more often than not, though the aim runs a little below the middle and the edge gives way a little against the very best opposition — two honest wrinkles across a long career. The matchup tally itself sits squarely in the middle, which keeps the story grounded. A veteran regular who keeps the fight honest, year after year.

chenauto.text: Since 2018, CHENAUTO has built a game on patience and position: well above average on the whole, hard to shift in a straight fight, and unshaken when the opposition gets strongest, holding its own against the toughest foes. The aim runs below the middle, and the pace is unhurried — the two honest wrinkles in an otherwise solid game. More often than not, the matchup count leans their way. A veteran who wins by choosing the right fights.

chryseplanitiafox.text: ChrysePlanitiaFox plays at a gallop: well above average on nearly every count, quick to every fight, and still pushing when the fighting turns harder. The aim wanders — fewer shots land than most — yet the exchanges keep breaking their way, which says plenty about timing and nerve. The lifetime board paints a quieter picture than the matchups, but the matchups are the louder truth here.

chuange6.text: ChuanGe6 plays a bright, busy game: well above average overall, quick feet, and a matchup record sitting above the middle. Accuracy and headshots both run above the middle. The lifetime figures back the matchups up. A strong regular with a sharp eye and lively feet, still early in a promising story.

chillatex.text: Chillatex has been around since 2013, and the game bends their way more often than not: well above average overall, with a matchup kill-death edge to match and a lifetime kill-death line sitting higher still. They hold up fine against ordinary opposition and soak up punishment better than most, though the sharpest third of the field takes a visible bite out of their results. The aim wanders — accuracy sits below average — yet the headshots that land keep the tally healthy. A long-serving regular who wins the long fight.
